Hakim Naceur

Full Professor of Computational Mechanics

INSA Hauts-de-France, Université Polytechnique Hauts-de-France, Valenciennes, France

I develop numerical methods for thin-walled structures under severe loading: locking-free shell finite elements, shell-based particle methods (SPH and peridynamics) for large deformation, damage and fracture, and the simulation and optimisation of manufacturing processes, from sheet metal forming and clinching to metal additive manufacturing.

About

Biography

Professor in computational structural mechanics since 2009, working at the interface between numerical methods and industrial processes.

Hakim Naceur is Full Professor of Computational Mechanics at INSA Hauts-de-France. From September 2020 to September 2026 he headed the institute's Mechanical Engineering Department, a department of about 90 faculty members running three engineering majors and several master's programmes. He carries out his research at LAMIH (UMR CNRS 8201), the joint CNRS and Université Polytechnique Hauts-de-France laboratory for industrial and human automation, mechanics and computer science, where he co-leads the MSPRO research theme of the Mechanical Engineering department.

He graduated in Structural Mechanics from the University of Batna in 1993, received his M.Sc. in Computational Structural Mechanics from Université Pierre et Marie Curie (Paris 6) in 1994, and his Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering from the Université de Technologie de Compiègne in 1998. He was faculty at Compiègne from 2000 to 2009, where he obtained his Habilitation (HDR) in 2007, then joined the Université de Valenciennes, now UPHF, as Full Professor in September 2009. He has been Professor at INSA Hauts-de-France since January 2020.

His research covers the formulation of shell and plate elements, meshless and nonlocal methods for thin structures (shell-based SPH, peridynamic beams and plates), damage and fracture, homogenisation and multi-scale approaches for crash and impact, and the numerical modelling and optimisation of metal forming and additive manufacturing processes. He is the author of more than 100 papers in international journals, 9 book chapters, a monograph on shell-based peridynamics, and over 150 international conference contributions, and he has supervised 25 doctoral theses.

Research

Research themes

Eleven lines of work, each tied to publications and doctoral theses. Figures are taken from the corresponding papers and thesis presentations.

Meshless · SPH

Shell-based SPH for forming and ductile damage

A single layer of particles on the shell mid-surface with Reissner–Mindlin kinematics, a Total Lagrangian formulation and return-mapping plasticity. The framework is validated on the Wagoner deep-drawing benchmark and extended to micromechanical damage (GTN, MCK) for failure prediction in sheet metal forming, as well as to functionally graded structures.

x(ξ, ζ) = x̄(ξ) + ζ·(h/2)·d(ξ), W(‖Xi − Xj‖, h)

Huang, Jia & Naceur · J. Phys. Conf. Ser. 2025 (NUMISHEET) · Compos. Struct. 2025 · WCCM & ICCM 2026

Nonlocal · Peridynamics

Locking-free peridynamic beams and plates

Bond-based peridynamic Timoshenko beams and Reissner–Mindlin plates, with reduced and selective integration and mixed formulations that remove shear locking from very thin (L/t > 10³) to thick plates. These models handle frame structures, impact, and the transition to fracture without remeshing.

Bai & Naceur · Arch. Appl. Mech. 2023 · Comput. Part. Mech. 2021–2024 · Eng. Comput. 2023 · monograph, Cambridge Scholars 2024

Finite elements · Shells

Shell and plate elements with discrete shear projection

Quadrilateral plate and curved shell elements built on the discrete shear projection method (Q4γs family) with Batoz and Katili: deflection, stresses, vibration and thermal buckling of FGM sandwich plates, and a new curved shell element using pseudo-curvatures.

Katili, Batoz, Widyatmoko & Naceur · Compos. Struct. 2024 · Katili et al. · Compos. Struct. 2026

Optimisation · IGA

Topology optimisation of curved thick shells

Level-set topology optimisation on trimmed, non-conforming multi-patch NURBS shells, with a diffuse interface and Hadamard shape derivative. The result is a CAD-compatible surface, developed with École Polytechnique and Stellantis.

Hübner Scherer, Zarroug, Naceur & Constantinescu · CMAME 2024 · Struct. Multidisc. Optim. 2024

Processes · Forming

Sheet metal forming, hydroforming and clinching

Over 25 years of work on forming simulation and design: the one-step inverse approach (Fast_Stamp code) with Batoz and Guo for fast formability prediction, optimisation of blank contours, drawbead restraining forces and material properties, springback control by response surfaces, tube hydroforming, and solid-shell models for sandwich steel sheets. Current work covers shell-based SPH for deep drawing with ductile damage, and machine-learning surrogates with inverse methods for clinching and riveting.

Naceur et al. · Int. J. Mech. Sci. 2001 · J. Mater. Process. Technol. 2004 · Comput. Struct. 2006 · Chebbah et al. · J. Mater. Process. Technol. 2011 · Huang et al. · NUMISHEET 2025

Processes · Glass forming

Blow-and-blow forming of glass bottles

Thermomechanical simulation of the blow-and-blow process with Saverglass, including temperature-dependent glass behaviour and heat exchange at the glass/mould interface. The interface heat-transfer coefficient, radiation included, is identified from experiments. The full forming sequence is simulated, and the predicted wall thickness agrees with sectioned bottles to within 10% at most measurement levels.

Cressin, Béchet, Moreau, Lochegnies & Naceur · Int. J. Heat Mass Transf. 2023 · SFT 2021, 2022 · PhD M. Cressin 2023

Processes · Additive repair

Repair of forming tools by wire-laser additive manufacturing

A multiscale, multiphysics model of WLAM repair of damaged forming tools. At the mesoscale, a multi-material volume-of-fluid model with ray-traced laser heat input predicts the melt pool and bead shape, validated on single tracks at 800 W. Its calibrated heat source then drives a macroscale thermo-mechanical simulation of the full repair cycle: removal of the damaged zone, deposition, cooling and final machining, giving the residual stress field in the repaired tool.

Chang, Jia, Boungomba, Naceur & Dubar · Int. J. Heat Mass Transf. 2026 · CFM 2025 · PhD H. Chang, with Prof. L. Dubar

Processes · Additive manufacturing

Metal additive manufacturing

Thermo-mechanical simulation of laser powder bed fusion and wire-laser deposition (multi-material VOF and ALE models), scan-path optimisation by surrogate-assisted genetic algorithms and deep reinforcement learning, distortion compensation, and the energy absorption of printed lattices. Applications include the repair of forming tools by deposition.

Bai et al. · J. Manuf. Process. 2025 · Mater. Des. 2023, 2024 · Chang et al. · Int. J. Heat Mass Transf. 2026 · Jia et al. · J. Manuf. Process. 2024

Damage · Fracture

Phase-field damage and fracture

Incremental alternate-minimisation algorithms for phase-field fracture with penalty enforcement of irreversibility, applied to crack initiation and propagation in solids and plates, and compared with peridynamics and XFEM.

Tran, Rahmoun & Naceur · J. Mech. Sci. Technol. 2024 · CFRAC 2023

Crash · Multi-material

Crashworthiness and multi-material structures

Reduced multi-material shell models for laser-welded joints, validated against refined solid models of the welded specimen in its test jig and about 20 times faster, hybrid wood and aluminium connections, composite and FGM plates under low-velocity impact, and homogenisation of architected and biological materials under dynamic loading.

Arif et al. · Eng. Comput. 2021 · Boli et al. · Compos. Struct. 2024 · Li et al. · Polym. Compos. 2024 · Rahmoun et al. · Mater. Sci. Eng. C 2020

Crash · Surrogate modelling

Surrogate models of high-voltage connectors for electric-vehicle crash

Detailed solid models of high-voltage connectors are too costly for full-vehicle crash simulation. The surrogate replaces each connector by shell elements whose polyamide-to-copper section is represented as a functionally graded material through the thickness. It is implemented as an LS-DYNA user material with GISSMO failure and non-local regularisation, and calibrated on shear and tensile tests. In full-vehicle crash simulations at Mercedes-Benz it predicts the same connector failure as the real crash test.

E(ζ) = (Ep − Ec)·((ζ + 1)/2)q + Ec, ζ ∈ [−1, 1]

Ridene, Coutellier & Naceur · ECCCS 2021 · PhD M.S. Ridene 2021, with Daimler AG / Mercedes-Benz

Current directions

What the group is working on now

  • Differentiable solvers in Python and JAX for explicit dynamics and inverse identification.
  • Neural surrogate models for joining processes such as clinching.
  • Crash response of porosity-graded lattice structures made by additive manufacturing, from beam-level models to the full structure.
  • Coupling shell-based SPH with ductile damage models inside an HPC Fortran solver.

Code

Open research code

Research codes and benchmark scripts are being released on GitHub.

The group's solvers are written in Fortran for HPC explicit dynamics and in Python and JAX for prototyping and differentiable mechanics. Repositories with verification benchmarks (shell elements, shell-based SPH, peridynamic beams and plates) will be published progressively on the GitHub profile, together with the scripts needed to reproduce the figures of recent papers.
